identification.summary: Cyber Av3ngers (CyberAv3ngers) is an Iranian persona that CISA and partner agencies describe as IRGC-affiliated and that has claimed many attacks on critical infrastructure [S1]. It is best known for compromising internet-exposed Israeli-made Unitronics Vision Series PLCs in late 2023 [S1], for the IOCONTROL IoT/OT malware reported by Claroty Team82 in December 2024 [S3], and for a 2026 campaign against Rockwell Automation PLCs described in advisory AA26-097A [S5][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Cyble reports that the group claims to be behind power outages in parts of Israel since 2020 (a claim, not verified) [S7]. Government-documented activity: Unitronics PLC compromises from about 22 November 2023 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name per coverage of AA26-097A: Storm-0784 (Microsoft's own page was not retrieved). Other names listed in that coverage: Shahid Kaveh Group, Hydro Kitten, UNC5691 [S5]. Treat vendor cluster names as the vendors' own tracking until mapped; do not merge vendor facts without the primary reports.

attribution.sponsor: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Cyber-Electronic Command (IRGC-CEC). CISA, FBI, NSA, EPA and Israel's National Cyber Directorate called the actors IRGC-affiliated in AA23-335A [S1]. The 2026 advisory (AA26-097A) links the activity to the IRGC-CEC [S5].
attribution.confidence: Stated by government agencies in joint advisories [S1][S5]. Treasury sanctioned six IRGC-CEC officials on 2 February 2024 over IRGC-affiliated actors' Unitronics PLC intrusions; a State Department reward offer of up to $10 million explicitly named the CyberAv3ngers group [S4]. Claroty describes the group as believed to be part of the IRGC-CEC [S3].
attribution.basis: Joint government advisories [S1][S5]; US sanctions on IRGC-CEC officials and a later reward offer (per press coverage, not primary documents) [S4]; Claroty's attribution of the IOCONTROL sample source to the group [S3].

objectives: Disruption and psychological/propaganda effect against Israel-linked and US critical infrastructure. In 2023 the actors said they chose Unitronics PLCs because of their Israeli manufacturer, and displayed anti-Israel messages on compromised HMIs [S2]. In 2026 reporting, operators tampered with PLC project files and manipulated HMI/SCADA displays, causing operational disruption and financial loss [S5][S6].

targeting.notes: 2023 Unitronics targeting spanned water/wastewater, energy, food and beverage, and healthcare [S1]; the Aliquippa, Pennsylvania water authority was among the victims [S2]. IOCONTROL affected Orpak and Gasboy fuel management systems in Israel and the US [S3]. The 2026 campaign hit Rockwell/Allen-Bradley devices across US government services, water and wastewater, and energy; victims were not named [S5][S6]. Some Israeli claims (for example power outages and water stations) were not independently confirmed [S7].

capabilities.summary: 2023: access to internet-exposed Unitronics PLCs/HMIs using default credentials, then defacement of HMI screens, in some cases rendering devices inoperable [S1][S2]. Dec 2024: IOCONTROL, a custom modular Linux-based IoT/OT malware reported to run on devices from multiple vendors (including Baicells, D-Link, Hikvision, Red Lion, Orpak, Phoenix Contact, Teltonika, Unitronics); it allows remote OS command execution and self-deletion, and the deployment method was not determined [S3]. 2026: direct connection to internet-exposed Rockwell PLCs using legitimate engineering software (Studio 5000 Logix Designer), Dropbear SSH for persistence, extraction, modification and redeployment of project files, and HMI/SCADA display manipulation, per advisory coverage [S5]. A secondary report states CVE-2021-22681 was used and sources disagree on its CVSS score [S6]. The July 2026 advisory update reportedly broadened vendor scope to include Schneider Electric and Siemens PLCs [S5]. Tradecraft is largely opportunistic use of exposed, weakly protected devices rather than demonstrated zero-days [S1][S6].

campaigns.name: Claimed attacks on Israeli power and water
campaigns.summary: Cyble reports the group claimed compromise of Israeli electricity and water infrastructure (including Nahariyya and Yavne electricity facilities and water stations) and published video evidence; Cyble found some screenshots did not support the claims, and independent confirmation was absent.

campaigns.name: Unitronics PLC compromises
campaigns.summary: From about 22 November 2023 the actors compromised internet-exposed, default-password Unitronics Vision Series PLCs in multiple sectors, including the Aliquippa, Pennsylvania water authority, and defaced HMIs.

campaigns.name: US sanctions on IRGC-CEC officials
campaigns.summary: Treasury sanctioned six IRGC-CEC officials on 2 February 2024 over Unitronics PLC intrusions; a related State Department reward offer of up to $10 million named the CyberAv3ngers group.

campaigns.name: IOCONTROL reported
campaigns.summary: Claroty Team82 published analysis of IOCONTROL extracted from a fuel management system allegedly compromised by the group; a wave hit several hundred Orpak and Gasboy systems in Israel and the US.

campaigns.name: Rockwell PLC campaign (AA26-097A)
campaigns.summary: Joint advisory of 7 April 2026 describes IRGC-CEC-aligned activity against Rockwell Automation PLCs across US government services, water and energy, with operational disruption; updated 22 July 2026 with wider vendor scope (Schneider Electric and Siemens) and new indicators.

diamond.adversary: IRGC-CEC-affiliated operators using the Cyber Av3ngers persona [S1][S5].
diamond.capability: Default-credential exploitation of exposed PLCs/HMIs, IOCONTROL, legitimate vendor engineering software, Dropbear SSH [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Per secondary reporting, leased VPS infrastructure and EtherNet/IP (port 44818) access to internet-exposed PLCs [S6]; IOCONTROL command-and-control details not captured here [S3].
diamond.victim: Water/wastewater, energy, fuel management, healthcare, food and beverage, and municipal operators in the US and Israel [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Anti-Israel messaging and targeting of Israeli-made equipment, with IRGC-CEC sponsorship per government advisories [S1][S2][S5].
diamond.technology: Internet-exposed OT devices with default or weak credentials and direct remote engineering access [S1][S5].

gaps: Primary documents (CISA AA23-335A, AA26-097A and its July 2026 update, MITRE G1027, Treasury and State releases, Microsoft and Dragos pages) could not be opened; this record relies on search-result summaries and secondary reporting [S1][S5].

Microsoft's Storm-0784 mapping and the Dragos (Bauxite) and Mandiant (UNC5691) cluster definitions were not verified from the vendors' own pages; one search summary attributed such mappings to a Tenable FAQ whose date was not captured.
Initial access method and deployment of IOCONTROL were not determined by Claroty [S3].
Credibility of many Israel-focused claims (power outages, water stations) is unconfirmed [S7].
2026 victim identities, exact CVE use (CVE-2021-22681 reported only by secondary sources) and the Siemens/Schneider scope are unverified [S6].
Exact date of the State Department reward announcement was not captured [S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-reachable PLCs, HMIs and fuel management systems at installations, utilities and supporting commercial infrastructure are key terrain [S1][S3][S5]. STEP 2: The environment favors the actor because exposed devices often retain default credentials and open engineering ports [S1][S6]. STEP 3: Template is scan and access exposed OT, use default credentials or legitimate engineering software, alter project files or HMI displays, and publicize the result [S1][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic defacement and disruption of exposed US and Israeli water, energy and fuel systems, timed to regional events [S1][S5]. MDCOA is use of IOCONTROL-class malware or project-file manipulation for lasting physical disruption of supporting utilities [S3][S5]. Candidate indicators: PLC/HMI defacement, unexpected Studio 5000 or EtherNet/IP (44818) sessions from unfamiliar hosts, new Dropbear SSH services on OT devices, changed PLC project files [S5][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track CISA/FBI advisory updates and OT exposure of base and contractor utilities. (2) Authorities: remediation of non-DoD utilities lies with owners and civil agencies; coordinate through established channels rather than act directly [S5]. (3) Mission assurance: identify OT dependencies (water, power, fuel) of critical missions, remove PLCs from direct internet exposure, change default passwords and add access controls [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partner agencies and sector ISACs; separate persona claims from verified effects before reporting [S7].
